description:
Programme or Project Overview

Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) invites applications for a PhD on natural visual patterns, mental wellbeing and overheating resilience. The project studies how natural visual patterns in the built environment relate to human wellbeing, and how these insights can be combined with overheating-resilience strategies as cities adapt to heat.

The doctoral candidate will design studies that link visual-environment measurements with wellbeing outcomes, and connect the findings to building and urban design decisions that also address heat resilience. The position is embedded in the university's built-environment research, and the appointment follows the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement with a gross monthly salary between EUR 3,204 and EUR 4,051.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in built environment, psychology, environmental science or a related interdisciplinary field. Experience with human-subjects research, environmental measurement or simulation is an advantage, together with strong quantitative skills. The working language is English.

Highlights

  • Natural visual patterns in built environments
  • Mental wellbeing measurement
  • Overheating resilience in buildings and cities
  • Human-environment interaction studies
  • Design-relevant evidence for heat adaptation
  • Salaried PhD, EUR 3,204 - 4,051 per month (CAO-NU scale)
